summary: The Jensen Huang/Nvidia scandal keeps escalating (CA AG subpoena, SEC probe, congressional inquiry) and is today's biggest, clearest-gap story. Phone news is thinner than usual — no major launch or leak cluster — so the beat leans on Black Friday deal updates, a fresh Xiaomi 18 Pro verdict, a Samsung feature test and a leak roundup rather than forcing weak filler; phone still leads at 5/10 picks. Reddit crawl failed (403, one of several sources) but coverage elsewhere is unaffected. No story cleared the bar for 'breaking' today.

topics.working_title: California AG subpoenas Nvidia as Jensen Huang scandal widens into an investor-fraud probe
topics.why_now: FT, TechCrunch, The Verge and Wired all have separate angles on this within 24h (Techmeme p9/p11, TechCrunch, Verge podcast). California AG Rob Bonta issued a subpoena over whether Nvidia/Huang's China ties let sensitive chips reach China and whether investors were misled — on top of an existing SEC probe and congressional subpoenas. Memeburn has no coverage yet.
topics.angle: Skip the affair-gossip framing other outlets lead with and explain the actual stakes for US readers/investors: what the AG is investigating, what 'misled investors' could mean for Nvidia stock and the chip-export rules, and what happens next (SEC civil probe, board investigation).
